title: Superlativo: la peor crisis que... jamás

sections.content: El/la + noun + que + [subject] + jamás + haber + participle is a strong superlative pattern -- "the worst X that [subject] had ever [verb]" -- for making the strongest possible historical claim about scale. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: La Gran Depresión fue la peor crisis económica que América Latina había sufrido jamás hasta ese momento.
items.english: The Great Depression was the worst economic crisis Latin America had ever suffered up to that point.

items.spanish: Esta caída resultó ser la mayor contracción comercial que sus economías jamás habían experimentado.
items.english: This drop turned out to be the biggest trade contraction their economies had ever experienced.

items.spanish: La caída del comercio se tradujo en la peor crisis fiscal que estos gobiernos jamás habían enfrentado.
items.english: The trade collapse translated into the worst fiscal crisis these governments had ever faced.

items.spanish: Esta combinación resultó la prueba más severa que los Estados latinoamericanos recién fortalecidos jamás habían enfrentado.
items.english: This combination turned out to be the most severe test the newly strengthened Latin American states had ever faced.

sections.content: Jamás here means "ever" (in a superlative claim), not "never" -- it strengthens a superlative the same way English "ever" does in "the worst thing that has ever happened," and always pairs with the pluperfect (había + participle) in this kind of historical sentence.
